ref: When I survey the wondrous cross (1707), st. 1
text:
When I survey the wondrous cross
On which the Prince of Glory dy'd,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

ref: When I survey the wondrous cross (1707), st. 3
text:
See from his head, his hands, his feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down;
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet?
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

ref: When I survey the wondrous cross (1707), st. 5
text:
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine,
Demands my soul, my life, my all.

ref: Alas! and did my Saviour bleed (1707), st. 1
text:
Alas! and did my Saviour bleed,
And did my Sovereign die?
Would he devote that sacred head
For such a worm as I?

ref: Alas! and did my Saviour bleed (1707), st. 6
text:
But drops of grief can ne'er repay
The debt of love I owe;
Here, Lord, I give myself away,
'Tis all that I can do.

ref: Come, we that love the Lord (1707), st. 1
text:
Come, we that love the Lord,
And let our joys be known;
Join in a song with sweet accord,
And thus surround the throne.

ref: How sweet and awful is the place (1707), st. 1
text:
How sweet and awful is the place
With Christ within the doors,
While everlasting love displays
The choicest of her stores!

ref: Join all the glorious names (1707), st. 1
text:
Join all the glorious names
Of wisdom, love, and power,
That ever mortals knew,
That angels ever bore:
All are too mean
To speak his worth,
Too mean to set
My Saviour forth.

ref: Not all the blood of beasts (1709), st. 1
text:
Not all the blood of beasts
On Jewish altars slain
Could give the guilty conscience peace,
Or wash away the stain.

ref: Not all the blood of beasts (1709), st. 3
text:
My faith would lay her hand
On that dear head of thine,
While like a penitent I stand
And there confess my sin.

ref: There is a land of pure delight (1707), st. 1
text:
There is a land of pure delight
Where saints immortal reign,
Infinite day excludes the night,
And pleasures banish pain.

ref: Give me the wings of faith to rise (1709), st. 1
text:
Give me the wings of faith to rise
Within the veil, and see
The saints above, how great their joys,
How bright their glories be.

ref: Come, holy Spirit, heavenly Dove (1707), st. 1
text:
Come, holy Spirit, heavenly Dove,
With all thy quickening powers,
Kindle a flame of sacred love,
In these cold hearts of ours.

ref: Hark! from the tombs a doleful sound (1707), st. 1
text:
Hark! from the tombs a doleful sound,
My ears attend the cry,
"Ye living men, come view the ground
"Where you must shortly lie.

ref: Nature with open volume stands (1707), st. 1
text:
Nature with open volume stands
To spread her Maker's praise abroad;
And every labour of his hands
Shews something worthy of a God.

ref: Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme (1707), st. 1
text:
Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme,
And speak some boundless thing,
The mighty works, or mightier name
Of our eternal King.

ref: How condescending and how kind (1709), st. 1
text:
How condescending and how kind
Was God's eternal Son!
Our misery reach'd his heavenly mind,
And pity brought him down.

ref: With joy we meditate the grace (1709), st. 1
text:
With joy we meditate the grace
Of our High Priest above;
His heart is made of tenderness,
His bowels melt with love.

ref: Why should we start and fear to die (1707), st. 1
text:
Why should we start and fear to die?
What timorous worms we mortals are!
Death is the gate of endless joy,
And yet we dread to enter there.

ref: The Lord Jehovah reigns (1707), st. 1
text:
The Lord Jehovah reigns
His throne is built on high;
The garments he assumes
Are light and majesty;
His glories shine
With beams so bright
No mortal eye
Can bear the sight.

ref: I give immortal praise (1707), st. 1
text:
I give immortal praise
To God the Father's love
For all my comforts here,
And better hopes above;
He sent his own
Eternal Son,
To die for sins
That man had done.

ref: Salvation! O, the joyful sound (1707), st. 1
text:
Salvation! O, the joyful sound!
'Tis pleasure to our ears;
A sovereign balm for every wound,
A cordial for our fears.

ref: When I can read my title clear (1707), st. 1
text:
When I can read my title clear
To mansions in the skies,
I bid farewell to every fear,
And wipe my weeping eyes.

ref: Great God, how infinite art thou (1707), st. 1
text:
Great God, how infinite art thou!
What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow
And pay their praise to thee.

ref: No more, my God, I boast no more (1709), st. 1
text:
No more, my God, I boast no more
Of all the duties I have done;
I quit the hopes I held before
To trust the merits of thy Son.

ref: Amazing grace! (1779), st. 1
text:
Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound)
That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,
Was blind, but now I see.

ref: Amazing grace! (1779), st. 3
text:
Through many dangers, toils and snares,
I have already come;
'Tis grace has brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

ref: Amazing grace! (1779), st. 6
text:
The earth shall soon dissolve like snow,
The sun forbear to shine;
But GOD, who called me here below,
Will be for ever mine.

ref: How sweet the name of Jesus sounds (1779), st. 1
text:
How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
In a believer's ear?
It soothes his sorrows, heals his wounds,
And drives away his fear.

ref: How sweet the name of Jesus sounds (1779), st. 3
text:
Dear name! the rock on which I build,
My shield and hiding place;
My never-failing treas'ry filled
With boundless stores of grace.

ref: How sweet the name of Jesus sounds (1779), st. 5
text:
Jesus! my Shepherd, Husband, Friend,
My Prophet, Priest, and King;
My Lord, my Life, my Way, my End,
Accept the praise I bring.

ref: Glorious things of thee are spoken (1779), st. 1
text:
Glorious things of thee are spoken,
Zion, city of our God!
He, whose word cannot be broken,
Formed thee for his own abode:
On the rock of ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose?
With salvation's walls surrounded
Thou may'st smile at all thy foes.

ref: Glorious things of thee are spoken (1779), st. 2
text:
See! the streams of living waters
Springing from eternal love;
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of want remove:
Who can faint while such a river
Ever flows their thirst t' assuage?
Grace, which like the LORD, the giver,
Never fails from age to age.

ref: Begone unbelief (1779), st. 1
text:
Begone unbelief,
My Savior is near,
And for my relief
Will surely appear:
By prayer let me wrestle,
And he wilt perform,
With CHRIST in the vessel,
I smile at the storm.

ref: Begone unbelief (1779), st. 2
text:
Though dark be my way,
Since he is my guide,
'Tis mine to obey,
'Tis his to provide;
Though cisterns be broken,
And creatures all fail,
The word he has spoken
Shall surely prevail.

ref: One there is, above all others (1779), st. 1
text:
One there is, above all others,
Well deserves the name of friend;
His is love beyond a brother's,
Costly, free, and knows no end:
They who once his kindness prove,
Find it everlasting love!

ref: Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat (1779), st. 1
text:
Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat
Where JESUS answers prayer;
There humbly fall before his feet,
For none can perish there.

ref: Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat (1779), st. 2
text:
Thy promise is my only plea,
With this I venture nigh;
Thou callest burdened souls to thee,
And such, O LORD, am I.

ref: Let us love, and sing, and wonder (1779), st. 1
text:
Let us love, and sing, and wonder,
Let us praise the Savior's name!
He has hushed the Law's loud thunder,
He has quenched mount Sinai's flame:
He has washed us with his blood,
He has brought us nigh to God.

ref: Safely through another week (1779), st. 1
text:
Safely through another week,
GOD has brought us on our way,
Let us now a blessing seek
On th' approaching sabbath-day:
Day, of all the week, the best;
Emblem of eternal rest!

ref: In evil long I took delight (1779), st. 1
text:
In evil long I took delight,
Unawed by shame or fear;
Till a new object struck my sight,
And stopped my wild career.

ref: In evil long I took delight (1779), st. 2
text:
I saw one hanging on a tree,
In agonies and blood;
Who fixed his languid eyes on me,
As near his cross I stood.

ref: I asked the LORD that I might grow (1779), st. 1
text:
I asked the LORD that I might grow
In faith, and love, and every grace;
Might more of his salvation know,
And seek, more earnestly, his face.

ref: Though troubles assail (1779), st. 1
text:
Though troubles assail
And dangers affright,
Though friends should all fail
And foes all unite;
Yet one thing secures us,
Whatever betide,
The scripture assures us,
The Lord will provide.

ref: Why should I fear the darkest hour (1779), st. 1
text:
Why should I fear the darkest hour,
Or tremble at the tempter's pow'r?
Jesus vouchsafes to be my tow'r.

ref: Precious Bible! what a treasure (1779), st. 1
text:
Precious Bible! what a treasure
Does the word of God afford?
All I want for life or pleasure,
FOOD and MED'CINE, SHIELD and SWORD:
Let the world account me poor,
Having this I need no more.

ref: Quiet, Lord, my froward heart (1779), st. 1
text:
Quiet, LORD, my froward heart,
Make me teachable and mild,
Upright, simple, free from art,
Make me as a weaned child:
From distrust and envy free,
Pleased with all that pleases thee.

ref: Come, my soul, thy suit prepare (1779), st. 1
text:
Come, my soul, thy suit prepare,
Jesus loves to answer prayer,
He himself has bid thee pray,
Therefore will not say thee nay.

ref: Come, my soul, thy suit prepare (1779), st. 2
text:
Thou art coming to a King,
Large petitions with thee bring;
For his grace and pow'r are such,
None can ever ask too much.

ref: Physician of my sin-sick soul (1779), st. 1
text:
Physician of my sin-sick soul,
To thee I bring my case;
My raging malady control,
And heal me by thy grace.

ref: God moves in a mysterious way (1774), st. 1
text:
God moves in a mysterious way,
His wonders to perform;
He plants his footsteps in the sea,
And rides upon the storm.

ref: God moves in a mysterious way (1774), st. 2
text:
Deep in unfathomable mines
Of never failing skill
He treasures up his bright designs,
And works his sovereign will.

ref: God moves in a mysterious way (1774), st. 3
text:
Ye fearful saints fresh courage take,
The clouds ye so much dread
Are big with mercy, and shall break
In blessings on your head.

ref: God moves in a mysterious way (1774), st. 4
text:
Judge not the LORD by feeble sense,
But trust him for his grace;
Behind a frowning providence,
He hides a smiling face.

ref: God moves in a mysterious way (1774), st. 5
text:
His purposes will ripen fast,
Unfolding every hour;
The bud may have a bitter taste,
But sweet will be the flow'r.

ref: God moves in a mysterious way (1774), st. 6
text:
Blind unbelief is sure to err,
And scan his work in vain;
GOD is his own interpreter,
And he will make it plain.

ref: There is a fountain filled with blood (1772), st. 1
text:
There is a fountain filled with blood
Drawn from EMMANUEL'S veins;
And sinners, plunged beneath that flood,
Loose all their guilty stains.

ref: There is a fountain filled with blood (1772), st. 2
text:
The dying thief rejoiced to see
That fountain in his day;
And there have I, as vile as he,
Washed all my sins away.

ref: There is a fountain filled with blood (1772), st. 3
text:
Dear dying Lamb, thy precious blood
Shall never lose its pow'r;
Till all the ransomed church of God
Be saved, to sin no more.

ref: There is a fountain filled with blood (1772), st. 4
text:
E'er since, by faith, I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply:
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.

ref: O! for a closer walk with God (1772), st. 1
text:
O! for a closer walk with God,
A calm and heav'nly frame;
A light to shine upon the road
That leads me to the Lamb!

ref: O! for a closer walk with God (1772), st. 4
text:
Return, O holy Dove, return,
Sweet messenger of rest;
I hate the sins that made thee mourn,
And drove thee from my breast.

ref: O! for a closer walk with God (1772), st. 6
text:
So shall my walk be close with God,
Calm and serene my frame;
So purer light shall mark the road
That leads me to the Lamb.

ref: Sometimes a light surprises (1779), st. 1
text:
Sometimes a light surprises
The christian while he sings;
It is the LORD who rises
With healing in his wings:
When comforts are declining,
He grants the soul again
A season of clear shining
To cheer it after rain.

ref: Sometimes a light surprises (1779), st. 4
text:
The vine, nor fig-tree neither,
Their wonted fruit should hear,
Though all the fields should wither,
Nor flocks, nor herds, be there:
Yet God the same abiding,
His praise shall tune my voice;
For while in him confiding,
I cannot but rejoice.

ref: Hark, my soul! it is the LORD (1768), st. 1
Hark, my soul! it is the LORD (1768), st. 3
text:
Can a woman's tender care
Cease, towards the child she bare?
Yes, she may forgetful be,
Yet will I remember thee.

ref: Jesus, where'er thy people meet (1769), st. 1
text:
Jesus, where'er thy people meet,
There they behold thy mercy-seat;
Where'er they seek thee thou art found,
And every place is hallowed ground.

ref: Jesus, where'er thy people meet (1769), st. 2
text:
For thou, within no walls confined,
Inhabitest the humble mind;
Such ever bring thee, where they come,
And going, take thee to their home.

ref: What various hindrances we meet (1779), st. 1
text:
What various hindrances we meet
In coming to a mercy-seat?
Yet who that knows the worth of prayer,
But wishes to be often there.

ref: Ere God had built the mountains (1779), st. 1
text:
Ere God had built the mountains,
Or raised the fruitful hills;
Before he filled the fountains
That feed the running rills;
In me, from everlasting,
The wonderful I AM,
Found pleasures never wasting,
And Wisdom is my name.

ref: The billows swell the winds are high (1779), st. 1
text:
The billows swell the winds are high,
Clouds overcast my wintry sky;
Out of the depths to thee I call,
My fears are great, my strength is small.

ref: To keep the lamp alive (1779), st. 1
text:
To keep the lamp alive
With oil we fill the bowl;
'Tis water makes the willow thrive,
And grace that feeds the soul.

ref: Far from the world, O Lord, I flee (1779), st. 1
text:
Far from the world, O Lord, I flee,
From strife and tumult far;
From scenes, where Satan wages still,
His most successful war.

ref: O Lord, my best desire fulfill (1779), st. 1
text:
O Lord, my best desire fulfill
And help me to resign,
Life, health, and comfort to thy will,
And make thy pleasure mine.

ref: O For a thousand tongues to sing (1739), st. 1
text:
O FOR a thousand tongues to sing
My great Redeemer's praise,
The glories of my God and King,
The triumphs of his grace!

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: O For a thousand tongues to sing (1739), st. 3
text:
Jesus! the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
'Tis music in the sinner's ears,
'Tis life, and health, and peace.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: O For a thousand tongues to sing (1739), st. 4
text:
He breaks the power of cancelled sin,
He sets the prisoner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean,
His blood availed for me.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: O For a thousand tongues to sing (1739), st. 5
text:
He speaks, and, listening to his voice,
New life the dead receive,
The mournful, broken hearts rejoice,
The humble poor believe.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Jesu, Lover of my soul (1740), st. 1
text:
JESU, Lover of my soul,
Let me to thy bosom fly,
While the nearer waters roll,
While the tempest still is high:
Hide me, O my Saviour, hide,
Till the storm of life be past!
Safe into the haven guide,
O receive my soul at last!

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Jesu, Lover of my soul (1740), st. 2
text:
Other refuge have I none,
Hangs my helpless soul on thee;
Leave, ah! leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me:
All my trust on thee is stayed,
All my help from thee I bring;
Cover my defenceless head
With the shadow of thy wing.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Jesu, Lover of my soul (1740), st. 4
text:
Plenteous grace with thee is found,
Grace to cover all my sin,
Let the healing streams abound;
Make and keep me pure within:
Thou of life the fountain art,
Freely let me take of thee,
Spring thou up within my heart,
Rise to all eternity.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: And can it be, that I should gain (1738), st. 2
text:
'Tis mystery all! The Immortal dies!
Who can explore his strange design?
In vain the first-born seraph tries
To sound the depths of love divine!
'Tis mercy all! let earth adore,
Let angel-minds inquire no more.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: And can it be, that I should gain (1738), st. 4

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: And can it be, that I should gain (1738), st. 5
text:
No condemnation now I dread,
Jesus, and all in him, is mine!
Alive in him, my living Head,
And clothed in righteousness divine,
Bold I approach the eternal throne,
And claim the crown, through Christ my own.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Love Divine, all loves excelling (1747), st. 1
text:
LOVE Divine, all loves excelling,
Joy of heaven, to earth come down!
Fix in us thy humble dwelling,
All thy faithful mercies crown;
Jesu, thou art all compassion,
Pure, unbounded love thou art;
Visit us with thy salvation,
Enter every trembling heart.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Love Divine, all loves excelling (1747), st. 3
text:
Finish then thy new creation,
Pure and spotless let us be;
Let us see thy great salvation,
Perfectly restored in thee;
Changed from glory into glory,
Till in heaven we take our place,
Till we cast our crowns before thee,
Lost in wonder, love, and praise!

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Rejoice, the Lord is King (1744), st. 1
text:
REJOICE, the Lord is King!
Your Lord and King adore,
Mortals, give thanks, and sing,
And triumph evermore;
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice,
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Rejoice, the Lord is King (1744), st. 3
text:
His kingdom cannot fail,
He rules o'er earth and heaven;
The keys of death and hell
Are to our Jesus given:
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice,
Rejoice, again I say, rejoice.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Soldiers of Christ, arise (1749), st. 1
text:
SOLDIERS of Christ, arise,
And put your armour on,
Strong in the strength which God supplies
Through his eternal Son;
Strong in the Lord of hosts,
And in his mighty power,
Who in the strength of Jesus trusts
Is more than conqueror.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Soldiers of Christ, arise (1749), st. 2
text:
Stand then in his great might,
With all his strength endued;
But take, to arm you for the fight,
The panoply of God;
That, having all things done,
And all your conflicts passed,
Ye may o'ercome through Christ alone,
And stand entire at last.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Hark the herald-angels sing (1739), st. 1
text:
HARK the herald-angels sing
"Glory to the new-born King,
Peace on earth, and mercy mild;
God and sinners reconciled."

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Come, thou long-expected Jesus (1744), st. 1
text:
COME, thou long-expected Jesus,
Born to set thy people free,
From our fears and sins release us,
Let us find our rest in thee.
Israel's strength and consolation,
Hope of all the earth thou art;
Dear Desire of every nation,
Joy of every longing heart.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Come, thou long-expected Jesus (1744), st. 2
text:
Born thy people to deliver,
Born a child and yet a king,
Born to reign in us for ever,
Now thy gracious kingdom bring:
By thine own eternal Spirit
Rule in all our hearts alone;
By thine all-sufficient merit
Raise us to thy glorious throne.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Come, O thou Traveller unknown (1742), st. 1
text:
COME, O thou Traveller unknown,
Whom still I hold, but cannot see!
My company before is gone,
And I am left alone with thee;
With thee all night I mean to stay,
And wrestle till the break of day.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Depth of mercy! can there be (1740), st. 1
text:
DEPTH of mercy! can there be
Mercy still reserved for me?
Can my God his wrath forbear?
Me, the chief of sinners, spare?
I have long withstood his grace,
Long provoked him to his face,
Would not hearken to his calls,
Grieved him by a thousand falls.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Jesu, thy blood and righteousness (1740), st. 1
text:
JESU, thy blood and righteousness
My beauty are, my glorious dress;
Midst flaming worlds in these arrayed,
With joy shall I lift up my head.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Jesu, thy blood and righteousness (1740), st. 2
text:
Bold shall I stand in thy great day,
For who aught to my charge shall lay?
Fully absolved through these I am,
From sin and fear, from guilt and shame,

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Arise, my soul, arise (1742), st. 1
text:
ARISE, my soul, arise,
Thy Saviour's sacrifice!
All the names that love could find,
All the forms that love could take,
Jesus in himself hath joined,
Thee, my soul, his own to make.

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: O For a heart to praise my God (1742), st. 1
text:
O FOR a heart to praise my God,
A heart from sin set free!
A heart that always feels thy blood
So freely spilt for me!

witness.work: A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780; 1889 ed.)

ref: Morning (1827), st. 6
text:
New every morning is the love
Our wakening and uprising prove;
Through sleep and darkness safely brought,
Restored to life, and power, and thought.

ref: Morning (1827), st. 7
text:
New mercies, each returning day,
Hover around us while we pray;
New perils past, new sins forgiven,
New thoughts of God, new hopes of Heaven.

ref: Morning (1827), st. 14
text:
The trivial round, the common task,
Would furnish all we ought to ask;
Room to deny ourselves; a road
To bring us daily nearer God.

ref: Morning (1827), st. 16
text:
Only, O Lord, in Thy dear love
Fit us for perfect Rest above;
And help us, this and every day,
To live more nearly as we pray.

ref: Morning (1827), st. 9
text:
Old friends, old scenes will lovelier be,
As more of Heaven in each we see:
Some softening gleam of love and prayer
Shall dawn on every cross and care.

ref: Evening (1827), st. 3
text:
Sun of my soul! Thou Saviour dear,
It is not night if Thou be near:
Oh, may no earth-born cloud arise
To hide Thee from Thy servant’s eyes!

ref: Evening (1827), st. 7
text:
When the soft dews of kindly sleep
My wearied eyelids gently steep,
Be my last thought, how sweet to rest
For ever on my Saviour’s breast.

ref: Evening (1827), st. 8
text:
Abide with me from morn till eve,
For without Thee I cannot live:
Abide with me when night is nigh,
For without Thee I dare not die.

ref: Evening (1827), st. 13
text:
Watch by the sick: enrich the poor
With blessings from Thy boundless store:
Be every mourner’s sleep to-night,
